subject: Hyperspring dedicated capacity: memory & quantization impact

From: Samantha Lee <samantha@hyperspring.ai>
To: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated estimate request — long-context models and quantization

Hi Marcus,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Hyperspring is evaluating dedicated capacity for a new product line and we need a capacity estimate tied to a few model/usage scenarios before procurement. High level:

- Models: Llama-2-70B (FP16 baseline), an open 13B variant we use in prod, and an internal fine-tuned 13B.
- Typical request profile: 25 RPS steady state during peak (US biz hours), average 1.5 concurrent requests per user, spike to 120 RPS for 30 minutes expected on launch.
- Contexts: two modes — short (4k tokens) for chat, and long (32k tokens) for document summarization with KV caching.
- Quality/latency targets: p95 latency < 600ms for short context, p95 < 1200ms for long context (we can accept higher for summarization).
- Durability: must be in dedicated pool (no shared GPUs).

Attached is our usage CSV with session lengths and concurrency patterns. Could you share an initial mapping of per-GPU memory needs (KV cache footprint + model residency) for both 40GB and 80GB class GPUs under different quantization schemes (FP16, nf4, int8-ish), and recommend fleet size for a conservative starting commit?

Looking for a concise table and a suggested canary + baseline reserved capacity split.

Appreciate it — Samantha
Samantha Lee
Head of Platform, Hyperspring

Hi Samantha — thanks for the clear brief and the CSV. I'll run initial sizing with the infra team and return numbers tomorrow. Quick clarifying Qs that will materially affect the math:

1) For the long-context path, what fraction of requests keep KV cached state across multiple calls (i.e., session affinity)? If it's high, per-client KV residency changes the multipliers.
2) Do you plan to pin users to a single model variant (e.g., always use Llama-2-70B) or route between 13B/70B depending on request?
3) Any strict upper bound on allowed model stalls (fallbacks) vs rate-limited errors during spikes?

I'll include per-GPU numbers for H100 80GB-class and A100 40GB-class, and outline suggestions for quantization tradeoffs.

Best,
Marcus Lin

Date: 2026-07-01T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Hyperspring sizing — ask for calc verification

Team — Hyperspring (HYP-2026-0421) asked for a tight estimate for dedicated capacity. They have two contexts (4k and 32k) and three model targets (70B FP16 baseline, 13B open, and fine-tuned 13B). The CSV suggests ~60% of long-context sessions keep affinity across multiple calls.

Please validate my draft assumptions below and fill in the per-GPU concurrency numbers:

Assumptions (draft):
- 25 RPS steady peak -> we plan for 1.6x headroom -> provision for 40 RPS baseline concurrency considerations.
- Average tokens per short request: 300 (input + output).
- Average tokens per long request: 5k per call, but with KV cache kept across session; effective new KV per call ~800 tokens.
- KV entry size per token ~48 bytes (key+value + overhead) on our runtime without aggressive compression.
- Model residency (FP16): 70B ~ 140GB, 13B ~ 26GB.
- Quantization multipliers: nf4 ~ 0.5x FP16, int8 ~ 0.35x FP16 (approx).

What I want: a concise table showing memory breakdown (model + active KV per concurrent slot + batch scratch) and a recommended GPU class and count for a conservative starting commit + canary pool.

Thanks — Marcus

From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, soojin_lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-01T10:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hyperspring sizing — preliminary calculations

Verified the assumptions and ran quick back-of-envelope numbers. Summary below — feel free to copy into a table for the customer-facing doc.

Key constants used:
- KV token size: 48 bytes
- Batch scratch overhead per concurrent slot: 6 GB for 70B (FP16) at moderate batch sizes and sequence lengths; 1.2 GB for 13B variants.
- Model residency baseline numbers (FP16): 70B = 140 GB, 13B = 26 GB
- Quantized model multipliers: nf4 ≈ 0.5x, int8 ≈ 0.36x (includes some rematerialization overhead)

Per-slot active KV memory (32k context):
- If session affinity retained and KV grows to 32k tokens: KV bytes = 32,000 * 48 ≈ 1.536 GB per session.
- Effective concurrent long-context slots: provisioning math -> with 40 RPS baseline and 60% affinity, assume ~24 long-context active KV sessions at peak if split evenly.

Example footprints (conservative):
- Llama-2-70B FP16 on H100-80GB-class (noting 140GB model won't fit raw): requires model sharding across 2x 80GB GPUs (model residency with activation offload) OR quantized to nf4/int8 to fit single 80GB with some offload. Practical deployment options:
  - Option A (80GB H100, nf4): model ~70GB + active KV + scratch => per-GPU footprint ~80 GB used, but you still need 1–2 GPUs for headroom; one GPU can host multiple smaller shards with worker-coordination. For simplicity -> estimate 2x 80GB GPUs to host 70B with nf4 and handle ~6 concurrent short-context slots with batching.
  - Option B (40GB A100, nf4): 70B will need heavy sharding (≈4–6 x40GB GPUs) and will reduce single-GPU concurrency; recommend H100 path for 70B.

- For 13B models (FP16): fits comfortably on a 40GB GPU. With nf4/int8 it becomes ~13GB or ~9GB equivalent — room for KV and batching. Expect per-40GB GPU concurrency:
  - short-context (4k): ~20 concurrent short requests (depending on batching).
  - long-context (32k): KV per slot ~1.5 GB so safe concurrent long slots per 40GB GPU ≈ floor((40 - model - scratch) / 1.5) -> with nf4 13B model ~13GB, scratch 1.2GB -> (40-14.2)/1.5 ≈ 17 slots, but practical limit lower due to pipeline memory -> suggest 10–12 slots.

Recommended conservative fleet (starting commit + canary):
- For mixed workload with emphasis on 13B and occasional 70B spikes:
  - Reserve pool: 6 x A100-40GB for 13B capacity (handle steady 25 RPS short-context + long-context mix).
  - Dedicated 70B pool (quantized nf4): 2 x H100-80GB for baseline (supports lower concurrency but handles p95 SLO for long ops with caching); add 2 more H100s as burst/reserved for spike mitigation.
  - Canary: 1 x 40GB node for early traffic and canary routing to validate performance.

Notes and tradeoffs:
- Using nf4 for 70B reduces model footprint enough to avoid multi-rack sharding in many setups but does introduce a small quality/latency tradeoff; int8 gains more memory savings but may require extra rematerialization and slightly higher CPU offload.
- KV offload to host DRAM reduces GPU pressure but increases latency; for p95 targets, try to keep hot KV on GPU and cold KV on host.
- Autoscaling should rely on routing policies and graceful fallback to 13B variants for non-critical requests during spikes.

I'll formalize these numbers into a short table. If we plan to recommend a committed monthly reservation, map expected token volumes to committed GPU-hours and propose a 6–12 month ramp.

— Karthik
